answer: Attestation depth scoring: each identity's weight equals the depth of its trust graph, verified by signed vouch chains. A dune of unlinked fresh keys scores zero no matter how many are minted. The relic of any reused voucher is flagged and its subtree pruned, while karst-like hollow clusters of sockpuppets collapse once one link fails. Forging depth k costs k real, staked, latency-verified handshakes from distinct operators, so farming n identities costs O(n·k) real coordination, not cheap signatures. Depth scoring works because sybils must fake costly human-linked history, not just keys.
